      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",

        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",

    {
      "key": "review_6ac33e30ba3cd7082113f310_1791180346395",
      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views.       "key": "review_6ac33e30ba3cd7082113f310_1791180346395",
      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",
        "handoffReason": "",

      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.         "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",

        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",

        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",

        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.       "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.         "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",

        "requiredQuestion": "",

If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",

      "key": "review_6ac33e30ba3cd7082113f310_1791180346395",
      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",

        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",

        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",

        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.       "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",

    {
      "key": "review_6ac33e30ba3cd7082113f310_1791180346395",
      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",

    {
      "key": "review_6ac33e30ba3cd7082113f310_1791180346395",
      "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views.         "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",

        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",

      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",

        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.         "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",

      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics.       "title": "Expected Views / Engagement",
      "revision": 3,
      "data": {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "purpose": "Answer customers who ask how many views, engagements, clicks, reach, interactions or general results they should expect from their ads.\n\nThe purpose is to explain that ads results cannot be predicted or guaranteed in advance because performance depends on the content most times, while reassuring the customer that good content gives the ads a better chance of producing a good result.",
        "intents": "expected_results, expected_views, expected_engagement, expected_reach, ads_performance, results_prediction, views_prediction, engagement_prediction",
        "triggerExamples": "How many views will I get?\nHow many views should I expect?\nHow many people will see the ads?\nWhat result should I expect?\nHow much engagement will I get?\nHow many engagements will I get?\nHow much reach will I get?\nCan you tell me how many views I'll get?\nCan you guarantee 100k views?\nWill I get up to 50k views?\nHow many views can 60k give me?\nIf I spend 100k how many views will I get?\nHow many views will I get with this plan?\nWhat should I expect from the campaign?\nWhat kind of result will the ads give me?\nWill the ads perform well?\nWill I get good engagement?\nHow many likes will I get?\nHow many comments will I get?\nHow many clicks will I get?\nCan you guarantee engagement?\nCan you guarantee views?\nHow many impressions should I expect?\nWhat results are guaranteed?\nHow well will the ads perform?\nWhat result am I likely to get?\nCan I get 1 million views?\nWill this package give me plenty views?\nIf I do the 10 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 7 days package how many views will I get?\nIf I do the 15 days package how many views will I get?",
        "keywords": "views, engagement, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, results, performance, expect, expected result, guarantee, guaranteed views, how many views, how much engagement, how much reach",
        "semanticTrigger": "Match when the customer is asking for a prediction, estimate, expectation or guarantee about the performance of an ads campaign.\n\nThis includes questions about expected views, reach, engagement, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or general advertising results.\n\nAlso match when the customer gives a budget or plan and asks how many views, engagements or results that amount will produce.\n\nThe customer does not need to use the exact words \"views\" or \"engagement.\" Match semantically equivalent questions about how well the advertising campaign will perform or what results they should expect.",
        "whenToUse": "Use when the customer asks how many views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results they should expect.\n\nUse when the customer asks whether a particular budget or advertising plan will produce a specific number of views or engagements.\n\nUse when the customer asks for a guarantee or prediction of campaign performance.\n\nUse at any stage of a pre-payment advertising conversation when this question arises.\n\nAnswer the customer's question first, then continue from the existing sales stage without forgetting information already established about their service, platform, budget, duration, plan, quote or invoice.",
        "whenNotToUse": "Do not use when the customer is asking about the PRICE of the service rather than expected advertising performance.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking how long the ads will run.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking what advertising plan or budget Joshspot recommends, unless they are specifically asking what views, engagement, reach or results that plan will produce.\n\nDo not use for an existing campaign performance problem such as \"My ads are running but I'm not getting results.\" That should use the appropriate existing-campaign/support knowledge.\n\nDo not use when the customer is asking for actual historical campaign analytics or current campaign statistics. This entry is specifically for predicting or guaranteeing future results.",
        "preferredResponse": "We can't predict the exact views or engagement you'll get. Good content gives your campaign a better opportunity to perform well, but results are not guaranteed.",
        "facts": "The exact number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments or other advertising results cannot be accurately predicted or guaranteed in advance.\n\nAdvertising performance depends significantly on the quality and suitability of the customer's content/creative and the performance of the campaign.\n\nGood content gives the campaign a better opportunity to produce a good result.\n\nDo not provide a guaranteed number of views, engagements, clicks, reach, sales or other results unless an approved Joshspot service explicitly provides such a guarantee.",
        "requiredQuestion": "",
        "notes": "Keep this answer confident but do not guarantee a specific advertising result.\n\nNever invent a number of views, engagements, reach, impressions, clicks, likes, comments, leads or sales.\n\nIf the customer asks something like \"How many views will ₦100k give me?\", do not calculate or invent a view estimate from the budget.\n\nExplain naturally that exact results cannot be predicted and that content/creative quality is an important factor in campaign performance.\n\nAdapt the wording to the metric the customer actually asked about.\n\nFor example, if they ask about views, answer about views. If they ask about engagement, answer about engagement. If they ask generally about results, answer generally about results.\n\nKeep the response short. Do not turn this into a long explanation about advertising algorithms unless the customer specifically asks for more detail.\n\nAfter answering, preserve the existing conversation state and continue the appropriate sales progression.",
        "paymentBehaviour": "Answer the customer's question first.\n\nDo not introduce payment if the customer has not yet been qualified or given the relevant service/price.\n\nAfter answering, continue from the customer's existing sales stage.\n\nIf the customer already knows the service/platform and a price or plan has already been presented but they have not agreed to proceed, an appropriate progression question such as \"Would you like to proceed?\" may be added.\n\nIf valid payment details/invoice have already been sent and payment remains pending, continue according to the configured payment-pending progression rules.\n\nDo not generate an invoice merely because the customer asked about expected results.",
